About

Pipelines by day, silicon by choice

I'm a software engineer based in Bangalore, currently on Fujitsu Research of India's MONAKA team, building the data and performance layer for a next-generation ARM-based chip aimed at data centers. Before that, I spent two years at Samsung R&D Institute Bangalore re-architecting large-scale data lakes and ETL pipelines, and started out at HSBC building data-sync tooling between AWS and on-premise storage.

Outside of pipeline work, I contribute ARM SVE optimizations to Milvus's Knowhere vector-search engine, co-authored a research poster on accelerating Milvus on ARM presented at ISC-HPC 2026 in Germany, and I'm finishing an M.Tech in AI/ML at BITS Pilani.

Projects

What I build when no one assigns it

Open-source ARM contributions

Open source & ARM

Performance work that started on MONAKA: benchmarking TiDB clusters on ARM vs. x86, tuning TiKV's topology, and a local crossbeam-epoch backoff patch (YIELD → WFE spin hints, PINNINGS_BETWEEN_COLLECT, memory orderings) applied ahead of upstream review. That work fed five PRs back into RocksDB, the Rust concurrency ecosystem, and Milvus's vector-search engine.

  • zilliztech/knowhere #1209 ARM SVE kernel for INT8 L2 metric computation 2x faster retrieval
  • zilliztech/knowhere #1218 ARM SVE kernel for INT8 IP metric computation 2x faster retrieval
  • tikv/yatp #95 Fixed SeqCst ordering and false sharing in the scheduler +5% ARM64 TPC-C
  • facebook/rocksdb #14190 SVE enablement + runtime detection for ARM Linux builds (in review) up to 42% faster XXH3 hashing
  • crossbeam-rs/crossbeam #1328 load_consume swap in the work-stealing steal path −18.6% steal latency

Publications

Two papers, seven years apart

ISC High Performance · Germany · June 24, 2026

Accelerating Milvus on Arm: SVE-Enhanced Vector Search for RAG Applications

Mohak Goel, Varun Reddy, Adarsh, Abhishek Jain

Poster on integrating SVE-optimized distance kernels into Milvus's Knowhere engine, reaching up to 2x faster retrieval on IVF_FLAT, IVF_SQ8, HNSW, and AutoIndex, benchmarked with VectorDBBench on a 32-core AWS Graviton3 system.
